doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

title: Lightnin' Strikes with Lou Christie and The Angels
summary: Prompted by Lou Christie's obituary, he describes working out the record at the piano with The Angels and having Artie Schroeck orchestrate.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Speaking of “Lightnin’ Strikes,” this is from about two weeks ago, Lou Christie passed away. New York Times obituary and this – I’ll read a bit of it, a small bit. “February 1966 with ‘Lightnin’ Strikes’ chart topper marked by a sweeping arrangement by the producer Charles Calello featuring glimmering piano, ringing church bells, and radiant backing vocals from a vocal trio, The Delicates.” I think that’s really hip, that the New York Times mentioned the arranger.

Well we actually made that record at the piano. The group that we used were The Angels – Peggy Farina, they had the hit record, “My Boyfriend’s Back,” but we used them as background singers. And they sang on all the records I did with Lou Christie. And we would get together, because they didn’t read music, and we would work the record out around the piano. So before I would go into the studio I knew what the record was going to sound like. There was the one thing that I didn’t anticipate was the guitar solo. The guitar player did it as an overdub and he played the guitar solo on a bass guitar. And also, what I did was after I laid out the records I gave them to Artie Schroeck to orchestrate. Now Artie was doing my sessions. I said, “Here’s what we’re going to do. I want you to use the two baritone saxes, a bass trombone, the rhythm section, and here are the tracks. Just copy this and put it on the record.” So although I arranged it, he did the
orchestration. And the reason why I did it, as a producer I had the record made. If there was something somebody could bring to the table I wanted to have it.
Well he brought some low end to that, with –
